final_candidates.decision_summary: Proline at the core aromatic W17 gives poor structure compatibility (ΔlogP≈-2.4) and ~0 ESM-1v plausibility, indicating strong fold disruption. Aromatic core position ideal for knockout.
Very low backbone compatibility (ΔlogP≈-4.3, z=0.13) and ~0 plausibility; Pro removes aromatic packing and disrupts backbone H-bonding in the conserved W/Y motif.
Lowest compatibility among proline candidates (ΔlogP≈-4.7, z=0.10); Phe→Pro in a hydrophobic cluster should strongly destabilize the fold.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are clearly separated from alternates and further evidence is unlikely to reorder them.

history.rationale: Trp17 is a buried hydrophobic core residue in the conserved YWY motif; proline substitution removes core packing and backbone H-bonding, strongly destabilizing the fold.
W17 is in the conserved KILRKESYWY motif (PsaE P-loop-like region); proline substitution of a conserved Trp should strongly destabilize the fold core.

Low structure compatibility (ΔlogP=-2.44) and near-zero ESM-1v plausibility confirm Pro substitution at the core aromatic W17 is highly disruptive — exactly the desired destabilization. Retained as rank 1.
Tyr18 in the hydrophobic core cluster; proline introduces a backbone kink and loses aromatic packing, disrupting folding.
Y18 sits in the same conserved aromatic motif adjacent to G19D; proline here breaks backbone geometry in a critical strand.
Very low structure compatibility (ΔlogP=-4.25, z=0.13) plus ~0 PLM score; proline removes aromatic packing and breaks backbone H-bonding in the W/Y motif. Strong knockout candidate.
Phe40 sits in a hydrophobic stretch (VIVRF); proline substitution disrupts strand/core geometry.
F40 is hydrophobic-core; proline substitution removes favorable packing and helix propensity.
Lowest structure compatibility among prolines (z=0.10, ΔlogP=-4.69); Phe→Pro in a hydrophobic cluster should strongly destabilize the fold.
Leu11 is buried hydrophobic; introducing a charged Asp into the core should be strongly destabilizing.
Buried hydrophobe to charged Asp is a classic fold-disrupting mutation.
Charge burial gives poor compatibility (z=0.156) and ~0 PLM plausibility, supporting disruption; kept below prolines as Asp may be partly solvated near the N-terminus.
Ile32 in the GII hydrophobic core region; charged Asp substitution destabilizes the hydrophobic core.
I32 is in the VIVRF hydrophobic stretch; Asp burial should strongly destabilize.
Structure compatibility is essentially neutral/favorable (z=0.99, ΔlogP=+2.0), implying the position likely tolerates Asp — counter to the destabilization goal. Rejected.

rejection.reason: Structure compatibility is essentially neutral/favorable (z=0.99, ΔlogP=+2.0), implying the position likely tolerates Asp — counter to the destabilization goal. Rejected.

history.rationale: Gly53 in a glycine-rich turn (GSAGGL); bulky Trp substitution causes steric clashes and impairs loop folding.
Gly-to-Trp in the GG loop introduces steric strain and removes loop flexibility needed for folding.
Moderate compatibility (z=0.56) suggests the backbone tolerates Trp at G53 more than expected, weakening the disruption rationale; demoted.
Phe48 hydrophobic core residue; Asp substitution introduces an unsatisfied buried charge.
F48 lies in the GFSGSAG region; burying a charge at a conserved Phe likely disrupts packing.
Structure compatibility is high (z=0.80, ΔlogP≈-0.22), indicating Asp at F48 is tolerated by the backbone — unlikely to disrupt folding effectively. Rejected as too weak for the knockout objective.

rejection.reason: Structure compatibility is high (z=0.80, ΔlogP≈-0.22), indicating Asp at F48 is tolerated by the backbone — unlikely to disrupt folding effectively. Rejected as too weak for the knockout objective.

history.rationale: Val21 in beta-strand region (GDVGTV); proline breaks strand hydrogen bonding, destabilizing the sheet.
Proline in a likely beta-strand region (GDVGT) disrupts hydrogen-bonding pattern.
Structure compatibility is very poor (z=0.126, ΔlogP=-4.29), comparable to Y18P; promoted from rank 8 to rank 4 as an effective secondary-structure breaker.
Ile10 hydrophobic burial; Asp charge introduction destabilizes the core, though position is near N-terminus so effect may be milder.
Weakest candidate; I10 is near the N-terminus and may be solvent-exposed/flexible, so Asp may be tolerated — deprioritized in favor of stronger candidates.

rejection.reason: Weakest candidate; I10 is near the N-terminus and may be solvent-exposed/flexible, so Asp may be tolerated — deprioritized in favor of stronger candidates.
